Executive summary

The quality of the GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_WAV_001_032 has been assessed by comparison
with observations and insitu data to describe the space-time evolution of the following
variables:

* Significant wave height (SWH)
* Peak wave period
* Mean wave Period/ Zero up-crossing period
* Mean wave direction

GLOBAL_MULTIYEAR_WAV_001_032 for the global wave reanalysis describing past sea
states over the years 1993-2022. This product also bears the name of WAVERYS and as such
it will be referred hereafter.

The quality of the WAVERYS wave reanalysis was estimated by: (i) comparing the SWH
analyzed with those measured by the altimeter of the HY-2A satellite (non-assimilated data,
open ocean, validation over 2014-2018);  (ii) comparing the mean wave parameters with
CMEMS in-situ buoy measurements (coastal data, validation over 1993-2015); and finally, by
(iii) comparing the time variations of these mean parameters with those of the ERA5 wave
reanalysis over the whole series. The quality assessment covers a subset of key wave
parameters, results of which are summarised below.

The core of WAVERYS is based on the MFWAM model, a third-generation wave model that
calculates the wave spectrum, i.e., the distribution of sea state energy in frequency and
direction on a 1/5° irregular grid. The wave parameters derived from the wave spectrum, such
as significant wave height (SWH) or the mean wave period, are delivered globally on a regular
grid size of 1/5° with a 3-hour time step. The wave spectrum is discretized into 30 frequencies
obtained from a geometric sequence of first member 0.035 Hz and a common ratio of 7.5.
WAVERYS considers oceanic currents from the GLORYS12 physical ocean reanalysis and
assimilates significant wave height observed from historical altimetry missions and directional
wave spectra from Sentinel 1 SAR from 2016 onwards.

For additional information regarding the in-depth validation of this product, the calculation of
the assessment metrics presented in this product other detailed information in quality and
noticeable events please refer to the reference quid document CMEMS-GLO-QUID-001-032
and the PUM.

Important notice:
The contents of this document are an assessment based on the best set of observations
available for evaluation at the time the operational system was validated. The validation
methodology was defined and agreed within CMEMS, inheriting the long experience of
MyOcean and MERSEA series of projects (Hernandez et al., 2018) The results presented in
this report and derived estimated accuracy numbers (EAN) are representative of average error
levels over large areas of the ocean. These numbers might be used as a mean error in one
given point of the area, but in order to refine error estimates locally, the reader is invited to
use complementary information from the reference QUIDs (error maps for instance, when
available).

1. Significant Wave Height

Significant wave height (SWH): For the open sea, WAVERYS performs with a global scatter
index of 8.5% with relatively low biases about 3 cm. The quality of the analyses is better for
tropical latitudes than for high latitudes where the scatter index reaches more than 10%. This
is particularly the case for coastal areas and/or those subject to complex oceanic processes
(e. g. instability of currents, tides, etc.), where the scatter index can reach 20%. Generally, the
wave model performs worse in light wind conditions (typically summer) than in strong wind
conditions that effectively constrain the model (typically winter), with differences of a few
percent on the scatter index.

2. Peak Wave Period

Validation of the following quantities is only available for a limited set of coastal moorings
located mainly in the Atlantic and Pacific of the Northern Hemisphere:

Peak wave period: Despite the difficulty of validation in coastal regime, the bias in peak periods
are about 10 milliseconds (ms). There is an area identified along the Iberian coast and in the
Azores with scatter index around 40% (compared to 26% of SI for all the measurements).

3. Mean Wave Period

Validation of the following quantities is only available for a limited set of coastal moorings
located mainly in the Atlantic and Pacific of the Northern Hemisphere:

Zero up-crossing period: We can note a bias of the mean wave period of about 40 ms, but
with low index scatter indexes, of about 15%. WAVERYS is particularly efficient at capturing
Pacific Ocean swells (scatter index of 11% in Hawaii).

4. Mean Wave Direction

Validation of the following quantities is only available for a limited set of coastal moorings
located mainly in the Atlantic and Pacific of the Northern Hemisphere:

Wave mean direction: The average direction deviation (bias) for all buoy measurements is
about 5° for a value of 38° of RMSD. Smaller differences can be noted in the Tropics, where
swell regimes prevail (differences of around 1°). Due to wave kinematics, the directions are
better constrained at the coast than in the open ocean.
